stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec. Describes a complex multi-locale (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature requiring full requirements elaboration (preview rendering, state sync, locale/brand handling, CMS integration) followed by testability, security, and edge-case hardening. Both agents assigned; openspec runs first, speckit reviews its output.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Live Preview plugs into the existing useContent/ContentstackContext/contentstack service layer. Contentstack is unreachable at test time, so VCs are framed with the client mocked. Three observable behaviours from the description: real-time updates, no full page reload, and operation across GO/UP/MX brand contexts.

Openspec provided an empty AC list but identified three core behaviours in their notes: real-time updates, no full-page reload, and cross-brand support. I authored the full AC list from scratch based on those notes and the story title/description. AC-1 and AC-2 cover openspec's real-time-update and no-reload behaviours. AC-3 covers cross-brand (GO/UP/MX). AC-4 and AC-5 add error-handling/recovery for connection loss. AC-6 adds a security gate. AC-7 adds accessibility. AC-8 covers rapid-update debouncing. AC-9 covers referenced/nested content. AC-10 covers session lifecycle. The original story description is extremely thin ('[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS' with no detail), so human review of my assumptions about scope is critical — particularly whether referenced-content cascading (AC-9) and session lifecycle (AC-10) are in scope.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: OpenSpec underperformed: it identified three core behaviours (real-time updates, no full-page reload, cross-brand GO/UP/MX) in its notes but left the acceptance criteria list empty and made no structural changes. Speckit then compensated by authoring all 10 ACs from scratch, effectively performing both elaboration and review roles. The collaborative pipeline did not function as designed — value was not non-overlapping; Speckit had to fill the gap OpenSpec left. The 10 authored ACs are individually reasonable and testable (real-time updates, no reload, cross-brand, error handling/recovery, security, accessibility, debouncing, nested/referenced content, session lifecycle), but the original story description is extremely thin ('[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS'), meaning several ACs rest on unvalidated scope assumptions. Speckit itself flagged AC-9 (referenced-content cascading) and AC-10 (session lifecycle) as potentially out of scope. Human review is required to confirm scope boundaries, validate that all 10 ACs belong in this story (vs. separate stories), and determine whether OpenSpec should be re-run with more guidance or whether the Speckit-authored ACs are acceptable as-is.
